paragraphs.en: In an additional scene, a fictional reader waiting for a short task thinks of a photo folder without opening it. A reminder, wanting to start and actually starting can be described separately. If a short break was planned, the same cue might fit the plan. One recollection establishes no cause, urge intensity or need to change.

Values 2, 4, 5 and a skip give sum 11 and mean 3.6667; adding 3 gives sum 14 and mean 3.5000, without evidence of improvement. Skips supply no zero or midpoint. Fewer than three withholds only that group’s personal values and interpretation; available groups remain. All insufficient groups still finish. Public general guides remain readable separately. Groups create no total, ranking, independent severity evidence or causal chain. Norms, reliability, validity, clinical and fairness validation are unestablished for this original bank and working English; other habit scales’ evidence does not transfer. Only page memory is used, without added drafts, personal sharing or analytics. Exit, reload, language change and history restoration clear answers. Fictional discussion needs no personal disclosure, repeated behaviour or habit change.

Another person might deliberately choose to consult a document and open the same page. Similar appearances need not mean identical starts. The mean verifies neither awareness timing nor harm or inability to choose.

The original arrangement, later choices, interruptions and effects need separate checking; a voluntary prior reschedule is another case. The mean converts to neither minutes lost nor a decision that this change was unacceptable.

paragraphs.en: In an additional scene, a fictional reader intends to stop browsing before a short task, continues, and later has less task time. The intended limit, actual sequence and feasibility of the plan differ. An earlier interruption might already have made the plan unworkable. One missed intention proves no lack of willpower and creates no requirement to stop the activity.

paragraphs.en: In an additional scene, a fictional reader begins a planned call late after browsing a collection and needs to understand the other person’s actual experience. Prior rescheduling, other obligations and duration of effects are not supplied by four responses. Missing values or a smaller mean do not rule out a commitment needing attention; a general guide cannot replace the people’s accounts.
